findings.claim: PRD still tells users to run `context-mode doctor --fix`, a CLI command, and says it deletes only one session's DB. ADR-0002 (accepted) replaced per-session DBs with one shared context.db per project; ADR-0010 (accepted, Q16) replaced the standalone CLI with the `ctx_doctor`/`ctx_upgrade` MCP tools, with uninstall as a mode of `ctx_upgrade`. PRD E19 was never updated after either ADR, so a user or agent following it runs a command that does not exist and would delete the whole project's shared DB, not a session.
findings.evidence: PRD-v2.md:84 '--fix deletes only that session DB (#867)'; PRD-v2.md:173 same text with issue ref; docs/v2/adr/0002-single-db-git-distribution.md:17 'One SQLite file per project' (no per-session DB left); docs/v2/adr/0010-doctor-and-upgrade.md:22 'ctx_doctor: read-only, one table row per check' and :42 'ctx_upgrade does not download anything itself' — both tools, no CLI verb anywhere in the file; docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md Q16 'Uninstall... is a mode of ctx_upgrade, not a separate CLI'.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: #867 (v1 mid-session SQLITE_CORRUPT report) drove the original per-session '--fix deletes that DB' design, before ADR-0002's single-db decision existed. ORIGINAL_INTENT: isolate blast radius of corruption to one session so other sessions on the same project keep working. REGRESSION_RISK: under the single-db model this intent is now backwards — the same fix step wipes every session and worktree for the project, the opposite of 'isolate'. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: any corruption-recovery rule for v2 must (a) name `ctx_doctor`/`ctx_upgrade` tool calls, never a shell command, and (b) rename the corrupt context.db/-wal/-shm aside (e.g. `.corrupt-<ts>`) instead of deleting it, so other data in the same file area is not silently lost and the user can recover it.
findings.fix: Rewrite PRD-v2.md:84 and :173 (E19) to say: on corruption, the tool result is a hard error naming the `ctx_doctor` fix action; the fix step renames the project's context.db aside and lets a fresh one build, not a per-session delete. Remove 'context-mode doctor --fix' CLI text everywhere in the PRD.

findings.claim: GS6 sets Claude Code's mcp_tool hook budget at p95 ≤ 40 ms wall, and command-hook agents at ≤ 20 ms CPU 'on top of bare Node' where bare Node alone already measures 45.6 ms p95 on the owner's Mac. Read together, every one of the 9 non-Claude-Code command-hook agents has an irreducible floor near 46-66 ms per hook call from process spawn alone, before any context-mode logic runs, yet the spec states the two numbers (40 ms and 20 ms-on-top-of-45.6 ms) as if they were the same kind of budget. No row anywhere adds spawn time to get one combined, comparable number per agent.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/TECH-SPEC.md:39 'GS6 ... Command-hook agents: ≤ 20 ms CPU on top of bare Node (bare Node alone is 45.6 ms p95 on the owner's Mac)'; tickets/verify-single-db.md:20 'Node startup alone costs about 28-37 ms CPU... Startup breaks the budget, not SQLite.' confirms spawn, not DB work, is the dominant cost for any spawned hook.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: v1's own hook-latency work (per verify-single-db.md citing #985-adjacent CPU investigation) already separated 'our code' cost from Node startup cost, finding startup dominates. ORIGINAL_INTENT: keep the DB/index logic itself cheap, which it is (0.8-1.0 ms per verify-single-db.md:20). REGRESSION_RISK: none from v1 — this is a new spec gap: v2 has not stated a single end-to-end wall-clock number users will experience per hook on the 9 spawned-process agents, so GP3's bench pass/fail line is ambiguous (is 60 ms a pass or a fail?). SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: GP3's bench check must gate on one measured end-to-end wall time per agent (spawn + logic), not on a CPU-only delta layered on a separately-quoted spawn number.
findings.fix: Add one row to TECH-SPEC §GS6/GP3 per command-hook agent: measured end-to-end wall time (spawn included), with a single pass/fail threshold, not two numbers the reader must add by hand.

findings.claim: DECISIONS-r3.md says the owner accepted 19 answers on 2026-10-14 but 'the ADRs, the PRD and the TECH-SPEC have not been edited yet' for most of them. Spot-checking the two highest-traffic items (ADR-0016 Case B/Q3, ADR-0002 Q6/Q7/Q10) shows those two ARE already applied in the live ADR text, but PRD-v2.md E19 (tied to the same Q7/ADR-0002 change) was missed. This means the 'doc changes still to do' list is not a safe inventory of what is left — some rows are done, some are not, and nothing marks which, so a reviewer or an agent cannot tell from DECISIONS-r3.md alone which of the 19 decisions still block downstream work.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md final line: 'The ADRs, the PRD and the TECH-SPEC have not been edited yet.' versus docs/v2/adr/0016-subagent-context-protection.md Case B row (already rewritten to match Q3) and docs/v2/adr/0002-single-db-git-distribution.md 'r3 decision' section (already added for Q6/Q7/Q10) versus PRD-v2.md:84/173 (not updated for the same Q7 single-db change).
findings.archaeology: Not applicable — this is a documentation-process gap, not a behavior change; no v1 code history applies.
findings.fix: Add a per-row status column (done / pending) to DECISIONS-r3.md, or re-grep each of the 19 target files and flag the ones still unedited (PRD-v2.md E19 at minimum) before the next review round reports them as fresh findings.
